page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, this instance features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled (2.0 threads per core) on an x86_64 architecture. The CPU includes 50 MB of L3 cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It is provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation and includes a 131 GB local SSD.

Benchmark data indicates moderate memory performance alongside weaker compute capabilities. The instance achieved average ratings in Passmark memory tests, Passmark database operations, and Redis SET operations, which reached 6.16 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also scored in the average tier. However, raw CPU performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and static web serving throughput all falling into the bottom 25% tier.

The E8s_v3 exhibits a clear tradeoff between high memory density and lower processing throughput. While its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU cycles, it is poorly suited for compute-heavy tasks. For example, LLM text generation with a medium 7B model is poor, registering at 5.03 tokens per second. Consequently, this instance is best aligned with workloads such as caching layers, relational database hosting, and memory-intensive data processing where RAM capacity is prioritized over raw computational speed.
